extracted.intended_audience: Congressional committee members, regulators, Volkswagen leadership, affected consumers, and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: Prepared statements and testimony for a congressional investigative hearing into Volkswagen’s installation of defeat devices and the company’s response. The document outlines expectations for corporate accountability, remedies, cooperation with regulators, and communications with stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency, cooperation, and clear, consistent communication
rubrics_metrics.description: VW must demonstrate "transparency, cooperation, and clear, consistent communication not only with this committee, the EPA, and other ongoing investigations, but also with its customers, suppliers, dealers, and the general public."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee expects regular, open communication channels (designated service line, website, micro-site, personal letters to affected customers) and ongoing disclosure as documents and new details emerge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate a serious commitment to answer questions and rebuild trust
rubrics_metrics.description: If VW is serious about rebuilding this broken trust, its leaders will need to demonstrate a serious commitment to answer these and many other questions prompted by its actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions will be judged by results over weeks and months; words alone are insufficient. Must provide substantive answers about what happened and how it will be fixed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full factual disclosure of actions, scope, and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear answers to: What did Volkswagen do to its cars? Why did they do it? Who knew this was happening (in Germany and the U.S.)? When did you know it and what did you do to fix it and come clean versus simply going along?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee repeatedly requests a factual account (who, what, when, where, how, and why) and expects documents and information to be produced as the investigation proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept responsibility and apologize
rubrics_metrics.description: Company leadership should apologize and "take full responsibility for what has transpired."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A sincere apology and acceptance of responsibility are expected as part of remedial steps; coupled with cooperative behavior toward authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide remedies and make customers whole
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept the consequences of the acts and provide a remedy to customers (including the view that every affected owner "should be able to get their money back, all of it").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies must be developed, tested, validated, and approved by authorities; committee expects concrete proposals on compensation, buybacks, or other consumer relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop timely technical fixes with testing and regulatory approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical teams must develop remedies for each affected vehicle group; these solutions "will be tested and validated and, then, shared with the responsible authorities for approval."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different vehicle generations may require different remedies (software-only vs. software+hardware). Remedies should be presented with timelines and disclosure of any effects on vehicle performance or fuel economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw and re-certify affected model applications when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Company withdrew certification applications (e.g., for model year 2016) and must work with agencies to continue the certification process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AECDs (auxiliary emissions control devices) or other software features should be disclosed to and approved by regulators as part of certification; coordination with EPA and CARB is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperate fully with regulatory, criminal, and state investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Cooperate with EPA, CARB, Department of Justice, State attorneys general, and congressional subpoenas and inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testimony under oath and production of documents are expected; cooperation includes providing requested information promptly and not hiding behind internal investigations excuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and hold responsible parties accountable
rubrics_metrics.description: "Responsible parties will be identified and held accountable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Company must conduct (and/or permit) investigations that trace responsibility; committee expects disciplinary or legal accountability where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct independent external investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Turn over the internal review to independent external counsel or investigators (e.g., outside law firms) to ensure impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External reviews (such as by an outside law firm) should examine systems and decision-making to determine how the misconduct occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine and strengthen internal compliance processes and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: VW will examine its compliance processes and standards and adopt measures to make certain that something like this cannot happen again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect organizational, procedural, and compliance reforms; meaningful changes to prevent future gaming of regulatory systems are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate and consider impacts on employees and local communities
rubrics_metrics.description: VW must consider "what implications these actions have for the thousands of Americans that it employs," including effects on plants and local economies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses should address job impacts, communications with employees, dealers, and local/state officials, and coordination with state investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear information on safety and legality of affected vehicles
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate whether affected vehicles present safety hazards and whether they remain safe and legal to drive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators and the company should provide an authoritative safety assessment; consumers must be informed about immediate safety implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept legal consequences including fines and potential prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress has statutes (e.g., TREAD Act) that allow for steep fines and criminal prosecution; VW must accept the legal consequences of noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Company statements acknowledge potential penalties and the possibility of enforcement actions; committee expects no obstruction of legal processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple, transparent communication channels to reach affected consumers
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up designated service lines, websites/micro-sites, and send personal letters to affected customers to communicate remedies and status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communication must be regular, clear, and reachable to customers, dealers, and suppliers; these channels should provide updates on investigations, remedies, and timelines.
